messages:
alex: quick follow-up from the operator handshake RFC — noticed a few edge cases where the Dedicated pool operator and control plane disagree on quota accounting

miriam: yep saw that in the simulation logs, some tenants get double-counted during rapid burst + drain :grimacing:

sam: can you paste the minimal repro?

alex: sure — repro is basically: tenant requests burst credits, operator pre-allocs ephemeral slots, then control plane wakes a scale job that also adds capacity. race leads to allocation > commit. logs: `operator:alloc=12 commit=6`

rika: ugh. sounds like we need a single source of truth for transient admission. either operator should be authoritative for ephemeral headroom or control plane should always reconcile before commit

miriam: my thought: keep operator authoritative for immediate admission (latency path) but emit a durable intent event so control plane can reconcile within X seconds and revoke if overcommit detected

sam: agree but need clear API boundaries. proposal sketch:
```
# admission API (fast-path)
POST /v1/pools/:pool/admit
body: { tenant_id, tokens_requested, mode: "ephemeral" }
response: { ticket_id, granted_tokens, expires_at }
```
control plane then consumes ticket_id, persists intent and returns final lease. If mismatch -> operator gets a revoke with reason
```
POST /v1/operators/:id/revoke
body: { ticket_id, reason }
```

rika: that avoids double-write, but what about prewarming? operator might prewarm before control plane has time to persist intent

alex: we can allow prewarm but make it idempotent: operator only spins resources when granted_tokens > 0 and records local short-lived lease keyed by ticket_id. If control plane later denies, operator must drain gracefully within grace window and mark tenant as throttled

miriam: need telemetry flags: ticket_state (granted/pending/denied), reconcile_latency, revoke_count per-tenant. ops needs alert if revoke_rate > 0.5%

sam: also think about cost fallbacks — if operator must revoke frequently, apply backoff and push tenant to a lower-cost lane automatically (quantized model variant or smaller batch sizes)

alex: one more surface: what about safety during control-plane partition? operator should be able to operate in degraded mode for N seconds using heuristics, but must refuse new long-lived reservations

rika: agreed. suggestion: degraded-mode policy opts: { allow_ephemeral: true, allow_reserved: false, max_ephemeral_per_tenant: 50 } and expose via /health endpoint

miriam: rollout plan: implement ticket_id flow + telemetry in canary, run for 2 weeks, gate on revoke_rate < 0.1% and reconcile_latency P95 < 3s before full rollout

sam: question: do we need cryptographic signing of tickets to avoid replay between operators?
alex: yes — sign with control plane key and operator verifies signature and TTL. small PKI shim in operator runtime

rika: implementation note: avoid schema churn — keep ticket payload compact: `{tid, tokens, exp, sig}`. keep verification code path audited

miriam: ok tiny UX ask: add a debug endpoint `/v1/debug/tickets/:tid` accessible to internal roles for postmortem

sam: +1. also add a synthetic test that fuzzes concurrent admit + scale events in CI for operator and control plane

alex: great — I'll write a short RFC addendum with the ticket API and degraded-mode knobs and a canary checklist. will ping infra team for PKI work

scale-bot: deployment-scan: flagged 1 canary cluster without ticket verification enabled — tag: needs-fix

rika: thanks bot, lowering canary until fix pushed :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all — follow-up RFC incoming, will include example curl flows and metrics to watch
